description: SASRec predicts the next item by using causal self-attention to select relevant interactions from a user's history. It combines item and position embeddings, attention blocks and feed-forward layers, then scores candidates against the resulting sequence representation. It can emphasize recent actions or longer dependencies. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781).
motivation: Sparse histories favor simple transition patterns, while richer histories support longer dependencies. SASRec learns which historical items matter. However, standard SASRec requires interaction history and learned item embeddings; it does not itself solve zero-interaction user or item cold start.
implementation_notes: Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset and preserve routing for all four categories. Use preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42 and the environment default SASREC_EPOCHS=200. Keep DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and artifacts beneath the trial directory. Select configurations using the pinned macro-average validation HR@10 only, within 43,200 shared GPU-seconds. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), measured metrics with definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Any architecture change must update both compatibility probes and the predictor writer. No benchmark results or concrete cold-start extension were supplied.
pseudocode:
For each category:
  Load the unchanged benchmark split.
  Build padded training histories and shifted next-item targets.
  Encode item and position embeddings using causal attention.
  Score positive and sampled negative items; optimize masked binary cross-entropy.
  Save model configuration, weights and dataset routing beneath the trial directory.
Run the pinned validation procedure and select by mean category HR@10.
Generate working/predict.py with the matching architecture and routing.

originality.positive: The original paper introduced an effective self-attention approach to sequential recommendation.
originality.negative: The supplied idea reuses the existing SASRec baseline and specifies no novel cold-start mechanism. Scores use a 1–10 scale.

future_potential.positive: Available titles and descriptions could support a future content-based extension for items with few interactions.
future_potential.negative: This extension is a proposal, not part of the supplied method; improvement requires measured validation.

code_difficulty.positive: The existing per-dataset SASRec baseline provides the main training and inference structure.
code_difficulty.negative: Architecture changes require coordinated checkpoint loading, predictor generation and diagnostic compatibility. Higher scores indicate greater difficulty.
